title: Accompanying Implementation Evaluation of the Browser-Based Digital Therapy Support Tool “Minime” in the KJ05 Adolescent Psychotherapy Unit: A Prospective, Single-Center, Exploratory Mixed-Methods Study Within the Context of Standard Care.
summary: Self-observation, therapeutic tasks, and the documentation of changes are central components of psychotherapeutic treatment. However, paper-based methods are sometimes difficult to implement consistently in everyday clinical practice and can only be integrated into the therapeutic process to a limited extent. This study therefore examines the implementation of Minime, a browser-based digital therapy support tool, into the standard care provided at the KJ05 adolescent psychotherapy ward at Aachen University Hospital. Minime enables the structured documentation of mood and symptom trajectories, thoughts and feelings, therapeutic tasks, resources, and therapy goals, as well as their integration into the psychotherapeutic treatment process. The aim of the study is to investigate to what extent and under what conditions Minime is accepted by patients and the treatment team, evaluated as appropriate and feasible, actually used, and integrated into therapy. Data will be collected using questionnaires before, during, and after implementation. The clinical efficacy of Minime is not being investigated.
conditions: No specific disease or health condition: implementation of a digital therapy support tool in routine child and adolescent psychiatric care.

interventions.name:

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients:
- Inpatient treatment on Ward KJ05 (pediatric and adolescent psychiatric ward at the University Hospital of RWTH Aachen)
- Intended use of Minime as part of standard care
- Sufficient knowledge of German to understand the informed consent form and the German-language questionnaires
- Sufficient capacity for understanding and decision-making to provide consent to the survey
- For minors: written consent from the patient and written authorization from the required legal guardians; for adults: their own written consent
- Age restriction of 12–20 years in accordance with the patient population of the psychotherapeutic youth ward KJ05; no additional age-based selection.

Specialized staff:
-  Employment at KJ05 (KJ05 staff of all professional groups) during the study period
- Potential involvement in the introduction, use, monitoring, organization, or management of the Minime implementation
- Voluntary written consent
Exclusion criteria:
Patients:
- An acute clinical situation in which, in the treatment team’s assessment, conducting an interview is not justifiable
- Lack of capacity to give consent or approval, or incomplete required consents
- Insufficient language skills without a certified translation available
- Regular use of Minime has already begun prior to the pre-assessment, such that the baseline assessment could no longer be meaningfully interpreted

Specialized staff:
- Lack of consent
- Exclusively very short-term involvement without sufficient exposure to the implementation
